description:
In an interview with Balance of Power, Sen. Pete Ricketts, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, says President Trump can use military force against Iran if needed, calling strikes one of several tools available in ongoing negotiations.

 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Ricketts Defends Trump's Authority to Authorize Iran Strikes

description:
Speaking before President Trump's State of the Union, Rep. Lisa McClain of Michigan acknowledges more work is needed to address affordability concerns.


 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. McClain Says U.S. Has "A Ways to Go" on Affordability

description:
Ahead of President Trump’s State of the Union, Rep. Pete Aguilar joing Balance of Power to discuss DHS funding talks, saying Democrats won’t support a deal without tighter ICE oversight.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Aguilar Says DHS Deal Hinges on ICE Oversight

description: Stephanie Kelton, professor of public policy and economics at Stony Brook University, discusses potential economic proposals in the upcoming State of the Union address. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on The Close (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Chasing Affordability in Race to Midterms: Kelton

author: Myles Miller
description: A whistleblower told Democrats on the Senate Judiciary committee that FBI agents had to drive through a winter storm overnight from Quantico, Virginia to Providence, Rhode Island to process evidence at a mass shooting scene because Director Kash Patel’s personal travel had left the bureau without an available plane.
title: FBI Director’s Jet Use Delayed Brown Response, Whisteblower Says

author: Miles J. Herszenhorn
description: If you want to know what’s going to happen to the 10-year Treasury note’s yield, watch the price of oil.
title: Treasury Yields React Mainly to Oil Shocks, Deutsche Bank Say

author: Maggie Eastland
description: Nvidia Corp. has yet to sell any of its H200 chips to China two months after President Donald Trump’s decision to allow shipments of the artificial intelligence processors to the world’s second-largest economy, according to a US official who helps enforce export controls.
title: Nvidia Has Sold Zero H200s to China, Top US Export Enforcer Says

author: Eric Martin
description: The Trump administration plans to reassure energy companies that they can sell oil and fuel to private Cuban businesses, after a renewed US pressure campaign spurred warnings of a humanitarian crisis on the island.
title: US to Reassure Oil Firms on Private Cuba Sales as Crisis Worsens

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Jamie Tarabay, Eric Martin
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe briefed senior lawmakers about Iran Tuesday, amid growing demands for the White House to explain its rationale for a massive military buildup that’s fueled speculation of impending attack.
title: Trump Officials Briefed Lawmakers on Iran as US Weighs Strikes

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: The president is expected to tout cheaper gasoline as Democrats point to power prices.
title: Trump’s Speech Set to Preview Midterms With Sparring on Energy

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The US abstained from a UN vote supporting a lasting peace in Ukraine, prompting criticism from President Donald Trump’s former Ukraine envoy.
title: US Abstention on UN’s Ukraine Peace Vote Prompt’s Ex-Envoy’s Ire

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon seeing pre-2008 crisis parallels amid AI and private credit scares with Bloomberg's Katherine Doherty. Then, Lauren Goodwin, Economist and Chief Market Strategist at New York Life Investments, weighs in on the latest Fedspeak from Fed Governor Chris Waller and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee. Plus, Bloomberg Tech Co-Host Ed Ludlow has the latest on Meta and AMD's partnership. Finally, Betterment CEO Sarah Levy weighs in on the platform's latest partnerships with Rate.com and portfolio managers to widen customer options. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: S&P 500 Rebounds, Anthropic Update Tempers AI Concerns  | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/24/2026

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Nariman Gizitdinov
description: Ukraine’s envoy to the US said the Trump administration protested its attack on an oil pipeline terminal on Russia’s Black Sea coast that disrupted oil flows from US energy majors in Kazakhstan.
title: US Warned Kyiv Over Russian Oil Port Attack, Citing Economic Hit

author: Lydia Beyoud, Olga Kharif
description: A senior US senator opened an inquiry into crypto exchange Binance Holdings Ltd. following news reports of its involvement in funneling nearly $2 billion to Iranian government groups designated as terrorist organizations and helping to evade US sanctions on Russian oil.
title: Senator Opens Binance Probe Into Alleged Iran, Russia Violations

author: Zoe Tillman
description: A group of small businesses that successfully challenged President Donald Trump’s global tariffs before the US Supreme Court have asked lower courts to reopen the legal proceedings so that they can begin the process of seeking refunds from the government.
title: Importers Launch Tariff Refund Process After Supreme Court Win

author: K Oanh Ha, Naomi Ng, Yang Yang (News)
description: Trade partners across Asia are reacting to the Supreme Court’s ruling on Trump’s tariffs: We look at the impact on pending deals and the US-China summit on the Big Take Asia podcast.
title: After Trump's Major Tariff Setback, The World Asks: What Now?

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss President Donald Trump's State of the Union address Tuesday night. On today's show, former White House Director of Legislative Affairs Marc Short, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Republican Senator Ted Budd of North Carolina and Center for Strategic and International Studies Senior Adviser Gregory Allen. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump To Make Economic Pitch | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/24/2026

author: Joe Lovinger
description: US Representative Tony Gonzales is facing calls to resign as he tries to fend off a serious Republican primary challenge amid allegations that he had an affair with a staffer who later died by suicide.
title: Scandal in Texas After Aide’s Suicide Roils Congressional Race

author: Catherine Lucey, Katanga Johnson
description: The Trump administration is discussing an executive order designed to force banks to collect citizenship data alongside other identification information from customers, according to multiple media reports.
title: US Weighs Bank Citizenship Data Requirements, Reports Say

author: Joe Mayes
description: Lawyers acting for Peter Mandelson, the former UK ambassador to Washington who was linked to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, said his arrest at home was prompted by a “baseless” suggestion that he was about to flee the country.
title: Mandelson Arrest Driven by ‘Baseless’ Flee Fear, His Lawyers Say

author: Allyson Versprille
description: The US House of Representatives voted down a Senate-backed bill that supporters said would improve aviation safety but was opposed by the Defense Department.
title: House Rejects Aviation Safety Bill After Pentagon Flags Concerns

description: From China to the EU, US trading partners are reacting to Trump’s tariff setback — and his threats to impose new levies. On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, Bloomberg’s K. Oanh Ha, Brendan Murray and Jenni Marsh discuss the shifting trade landscape and the winners and losers in Trump’s trade war. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Trump’s Tariff Setback Means for China, Global Trade

author: Petra Sorge, Michael Nienaber
description: The German government agreed to abolish a controversial ban on new gas and oil heating systems as Chancellor Friedrich Merz’ conservatives rush to deliver on a key electoral promise.
title: German Government Waters Down Controversial Heating Law

author: Jamie Tarabay, Chris Strohm
description: The Department of Justice appears to have withheld from disclosure files on disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein related to a claim that President Donald Trump sexually abused a minor, a top Democratic lawmaker said Tuesday.
title: Democrat Says DOJ Withheld Epstein Files on Trump Abuse Claim

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: Today on the Big Take: What Trump is expected to cover and what that reveals about his priorities and his grip on his party.
title: A Guide to the State of Trump and the Union

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Nigeria’s President Bola Tinubu has named a new inspector-general of police who will lead efforts to stem rising violence by armed groups, underscoring persistent security challenges in the country despite US military support.
title: Nigeria Names New Police Head as Violence Spreads Amid US Help

author: Kavita Mokha
description: French President Emmanuel Macron accepted Louvre president Laurence des Cars’ resignation Tuesday, saying it was an “act of responsibility” after a brazen heist at the renowned museum in October.
title: Louvre President Resigns After October Museum Heist

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel plans to make further trade concessions to the US on food and agricultural goods, as part of efforts to persuade its closest ally to ease tariffs on exports from the Jewish state.
title: Israel Plans to Boost US Wheat Imports in Bid for Tariff Relief

author: Samy Adghirni, Kavita Mokha
description: France plans to restore US Ambassador Charles Kushner’s access to French government officials after he told Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot that he he didn’t plan to interfere in French public debate, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: France to Restore US Ambassador Kushner’s Access After Call

author: Isabel Gottlieb
description: President Donald Trump has already leaned on alternative legislation to try to rebuild his tariff wall, after the US Supreme Court ruled that he can’t use a 1977 emergency law to impose import taxes.
title: Trump’s Options After the Supreme Court Said His Tariffs Are Illegal

author: Jim Wyss
description: Honduras became the latest nation to announce it will quit using Cuban medical workers, as Washington continues to choke off sources of funding for the government in Havana.
title: Honduras Dumps Cuban Doctors, Depriving Havana of More Revenue

author: Arne Delfs
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz sent a conciliatory message to President Xi Jinping as he departed Berlin on his inaugural trip to China, while urging the government in Beijing to help ensure “fair and transparent” rules-based commerce.
title: Germany’s Merz Reaches Out to Xi Before Inaugural Trip to China

author: Andrea Palasciano, Olesia Safronova
description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc will deliver on its €90 billion ($106 billion) loan package to Ukraine “one way or another” as the war-battered nation is set to run out of funds in a matter of weeks.
title: EU Chief Says €90 Billion for Kyiv Coming One Way or Another

author: Courtney McBride
description: The US military boarded another sanctioned oil tanker in the Indian Ocean after tracking it from the Caribbean, the Pentagon said on Tuesday, as the Trump administration continues to enforce a maritime quarantine around Venezuela.
title: US Boards Third Venezuela-Linked Oil Tanker in Indian Ocean

author: Zoe Tillman
description: US courts are foiling efforts by the Trump administration to keep under wraps information about the Department of Government Efficiency and the role that Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, played in it during his whirlwind stint with the White House last year.
title: Trump’s DOJ Losing Court Fights Over DOGE, Musk Secrecy

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: When President Donald Trump delivers his State of the Union address in the US Capitol, he will be doing so in front of a backdrop of a hobbled economic agenda, sinking approval ratings and fresh rebukes from his own political party.
title: Trump to Make Economic Pitch to Congress as Headwinds Grow

author: Okech Francis
description: South Sudan’s President Salva Kiir appointed Salvatore Garang Mabiordit as finance minister, the ninth time he’s replaced the head of the oil-producing nation’s Treasury in less than six years.
title: South Sudan Picks Ninth Finance Minister in Less Than Six Years

author: Paul Richardson
description: America’s new ambassador to South Africa struck a conciliatory note in a video message to the country that contrasted sharply with the bellicose comments by President Donald Trump.
title: Trump’s Ambassador Strikes Softer Tone in South Africa Debut

description:
The fallout from the Peter Mandelson scandal continues to cause a headache for embattled Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

Lizzy Burden explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Mandelson Scandal Causes Headache for Starmer

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: The focus of NATO’s air surveillance in Turkey has shifted from Russia to Iran as the risk of a US-led military campaign against Tehran mounts, people familiar with the matter said.
title: NATO Said to Step Up Iran Surveillance as Tensions With US Mount

author: Max Ramsay, Maciej Martewicz, Alan Katz
description: At least Bill White, Donald Trump’s ambassador to Brussels, showed up when summoned by the foreign ministry over some undiplomatic interventions into Belgian politics.
title: MAGA Meets Europe: Trump’s Envoys Rip Up Diplomatic Playbook

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union’s trade chief urged the bloc’s lawmakers to approve a trade deal with the US in March, as long as there is certainty by then on President Donald Trump’s new tariff plans.
title: EU Trade Chief Presses for March Approval of US Deal

author: Ott Ummelas
description: Norway’s trade minister indicated the nation isn’t walking away from a draft tariff deal with the US, negotiated last summer, even as President Donald Trump’s policy moves add uncertainty.
title: Norway Trade Minister Signals Draft US Tariff Deal Remains Alive

author: John Ainger
description: The European Union will on April 15 unveil a proposal to ban the remaining imports of Russian oil, just three days after elections in Hungary, one of the last nations still reliant on the supplies, according to a document seen by Bloomberg.
title: EU to Propose Russian Oil Ban Three Days After Hungary Election

author: Alberto Nardelli, Jorge Valero
description: European Union officials believe the US will soon streamline its broad tariffs on products containing steel and aluminum, a topic that’s been an irritant in transatlantic relations and a key sticking point in trade negotiations.
title: EU Sees US Easing Impact of Metals Tariffs in Coming Weeks

author: Julian Lee
description: Increases in seaborne flows make up for lost piped volumes to Hungary, Slovakia
title: Russia’s Crude Shipments Scrape Gain to Offset Pipeline Losses

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spain’s government is trying to cap how much revenue media outlets can receive from public-sector advertising, saying the measure is intended to combat disinformation.
title: Spain Seeks to Limit How Much Taxpayer Ad Money Goes to Media

author: Ellen Milligan
description: Mounting Russian casualties are likely to hinder President Vladimir Putin’s ability to launch a large-scale offensive against Ukraine in the coming months, according to Western officials.
title: Russian Offensive Hampered by Losses, Western Officials Say

author: Maya Averbuch, Andrea Navarro
description: The killing of “El Mencho,” one of Mexico’s most wanted drug lords, risks being both a blessing and curse for President Claudia Sheinbaum.
title: Mexico’s Big Cartel Win Also Risks More Violence Ahead

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump is set to highlight his administration’s efforts to ensure that technology companies’ buildout of energy-hungry data centers won’t raise electricity prices and cause other burdens for consumers.
title: Trump Seeks Vows From Tech Firms to Cover Data Center Costs
